issues.failure_explanation: By the proof of Theorem th:reduction_SVcones_anglescones, $\langle Uu,Vv\rangle=\langle u,Av\rangle/\Vert A\Vert$, so the critical values of $\MA(\wt P,\wt Q)$ are the $(P,Q)$-singular values of $A$ divided by $\Vert A\Vert$; the correct correspondence is $\arccos(\sigma/\Vert A\Vert)$. As written the claim is false whenever $\Vert A\Vert\ne1$ and can even be undefined: e.g. for $A=2I$, $P=Q=\R^2_+$, $\sigma=2$ is a $(P,Q)$-singular value, the lifted critical angle is $\arccos(1)=0$, while $\arccos(2)$ does not exist.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\sigma$ is a $(P,Q)$-singular value of $A$ if and only if $\arccos(\sigma)$ is a critical angle between $\wt P$ and $\wt Q$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\arccos(\sigma)$ by $\arccos(\sigma/\Vert A\Vert)$, i.e. state that the critical values of $\MA(\wt P,\wt Q)$ are the $(P,Q)$-singular values of $\Vert A\Vert^{-1}A$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated correspondence between $(P,Q)$-singular values of $A$ and critical angles between $\wt P$ and $\wt Q$ is incorrect (possibly undefined) for $\Vert A\Vert\ne1$; a reader using it obtains wrong angles. No labelled result relies on this sentence (Corollary cor:saddle_ConeSV uses only the critical-pair correspondence, which is correct).
issues.title: Wrong singular-value-to-angle correspondence in remark (missing 1/||A|| factor)
issues.why_classification: A one-line normalization correction removes the falsehood with no mathematical loss; nothing downstream depends on the sentence.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let us define the \textit{Nash pairs} $(u^*, v^*)\in P\times Q$ of the problem $\SV(A,P,Q)$ as the unit vectors such that
Therefore, since any solution pair is a Nash pair we have that if $(u,v)$ is a solution pair of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ then $u=g_i$ and $v=h_j$ for some $i,j$

issues.failure_explanation: A Nash pair must be globally optimal in each block, which local minima need not be. Counterexample: $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, $P=Q=\R^2_+$. The pair $(e_1,e_1)$ is a critical pair and a strict local minimum with value $2$ (with $u=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$, $v=(\cos\phi,\sin\phi)$ the objective $2\cos\theta\cos\phi+\cos\theta\sin\phi+\sin\theta\cos\phi+\sin\theta\sin\phi>2$ for all small $\theta,\phi>0$), but it is not a Nash pair since $\langle e_2,Ae_1\rangle=1<2$, i.e. $u^*=e_1$ does not minimize $\langle u,Ae_1\rangle$ over unit $u\in P$ (the minimizer is $e_2$). Only the solution-pair part of the claim is correct.

failure_location.quote: Observe also that any solution pair and all local minima of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ are Nash pairs.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to solution pairs ('any solution pair of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ is a Nash pair'), or state it only for local minima with negative value of the norm-relaxed problem, where block-wise global optimality does hold.
issues.overall_effect: The observation is false as stated; any analysis treating local minima as block-wise globally optimal is unsound. Proposition pro:nonnegative_case_SVcones uses only the correct solution-pair part, so no labelled result or algorithm is invalidated.
issues.title: False claim that all local minima of SV(A,P,Q) are Nash pairs
issues.why_classification: A one-line restriction of the claim removes the falsehood; no theorem, algorithm or guarantee relies on the local-minima part.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: {Observe that $-\Vert A\Vert\leq \langle u,Av\rangle\leq\Vert A\Vert$ for all feasible pair $(u,v)$ of $\SV(A,P,Q)$.}

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed equivalence fails in the sufficiency direction. If $P=\R_+g$ and $Q=\R_+h$, the only feasible pair is $(g,h)$ and the optimal value is $\langle g,Ah\rangle$, which can be strictly smaller than $\Vert A\Vert$. Counterexample: $P=Q=\R_+e_1\subset\R^2$, $A=\mathrm{diag}(1,5)$: both cones have a single generator and $G^\top AH=[1]\ge0$, yet the unique feasible pair gives $\langle u,Av\rangle=1\ne5=\Vert A\|$. (Necessity holds: an optimal value of $\Vert A\Vert$ forces all feasible values to equal $\Vert A\Vert$, hence $P,Q$ are single rays with $\langle g,Ah\rangle=\Vert A\Vert$.)

failure_location.quote: However, the case $\langle u, Av\rangle = \|A\|$ is easy to check, since it is equivalent to say that both $P,Q$ have only one generator and $G^\top AH$ is a $1\times 1$ nonnegative matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the characterization, e.g. '$\lambda^*=\Vert A\Vert$ iff $P$ and $Q$ are single rays whose generators satisfy $\langle g,Ah\rangle=\Vert A\Vert$', or note that the case is subsumed by the $G^\top AH\ge0$ preprocessing.
issues.overall_effect: The stated 'easy check' for the case $\lambda^*=\Vert A\Vert$ misidentifies instances: single-ray cones with $0\le\langle g,Ah\rangle<\Vert A\Vert$ would be wrongly declared to have optimal value $\Vert A\Vert$. Since the pipeline of Section 4.1 detects this case anyway via the check $G^\top AH\ge0$, no algorithm or labelled result is affected.
issues.title: Incorrect characterization of the case <u,Av> = ||A||
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the characterization (adding the equality $\langle g,Ah\rangle=\Vert A\Vert$) preserves all claims; the case is anyway handled by the existing preprocessing.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let  $(u,v)$ be a local minimum of $\MA(P,  Q)$ with $u \neq -v$ in dimension $n\le 3$. Then $u$ or $v$ is a generator of its respective cone.
As a consequence, the minimum over the optimal values of $\MA(\f R_+g_i,Q)$ and $\MA(P,\f R_+ h_j)$ over all $i,j$ correspond to the maximum angle of $\MA(P, Q)$.
Notice that this case coincides with the condition $P\cap (-Q)\ne \{0\}$ when $A=I$.

issues.failure_explanation: Corollary cor:local_minimum_angles_have_generators_in_dim3 holds only under the hypothesis $u\neq-v$, but the prose drops this hypothesis and concludes that every solution pair in dimension $\le3$ contains a generator, and hence that the maximum angle is found by minimizing over the ray-restricted problems $\MA(\R_+g_i,Q)$ and $\MA(P,\R_+h_j)$. Both fail when the maximal angle is $\pi$, attained by an antipodal pair off the extreme rays. Counterexample in $\R^3$: $P=\mathrm{cone}\{e_1,e_2\}$, $Q=\mathrm{cone}\{(-1,-1,1),(-1,-1,-1)\}$. The unique optimal pair is $u^*=(1,1,0)/\sqrt2\in P$, $v^*=-u^*\in Q$ with $\langle u^*,v^*\rangle=-1$; neither vector is on a ray of its cone, and the ray enumeration only yields $-1/\sqrt2$ and $-\sqrt{2/3}\approx-0.816$, not $-1$.

failure_location.quote: Corollary~\ref{cor:local_minimum_angles_have_generators_in_dim3} tells us that any solution $(u^*,v^*)$ of $\MA(P, Q)$ in dimension $3$ or less contains at least a generator.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the antipodal check $P\cap(-Q)\ne\{0\}$ (maximal angle $\pi$, checkable in polynomial time; the paper itself notes this condition for $A=I$ in Section 3.2) and state the generator-enumeration reduction only for instances with $P\cap(-Q)=\{0\}$.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed reduction of $\MA(P,Q)$ in dimension $\le3$ to generator-ray subproblems is invalid when the maximal angle is $\pi$ attained off rays, and the paragraph's coverage claim ('all solution pairs contain a generator') is false. The subproblems \eqref{eq:angles_cones_convex} and \eqref{eq:conic_sv_convex} remain well defined, and no labelled result depends on the false reduction.
issues.title: Dimension <= 3 generator claim and ray-enumeration reduction ignore the antipodal case
issues.why_classification: A routine additional check repairs the claim; the method, conclusion and advertised polynomial-time scope for dimension $\le3$ all survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
$\lambda:= - \sqrt{\rho(A_yA_x)}$ is the least eigenvalue of $ M:= \begin{pmatrix}
       0& A_x\\A_y& 0  \end{pmatrix}$

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses do not exclude $\rho(A_yA_x)=0$ (e.g. $\ol G^\top A\ol H=0$, which occurs for valid inputs such as $A=\mathrm{diag}(0,1)$ with $\ol G=\ol H=e_1$ in $\R^2$, $\mathcal I=\mathcal J=\{1\}$). Then $\lambda:=-\sqrt{\rho}=0$, so $V$ is defined through a division by zero and items 3-4, as well as their proofs (which repeatedly divide by $\lambda$, e.g. '$\ol y = A_x\ol x/\lambda$'), are ill-defined. The proof needs the omitted hypothesis $\rho(A_yA_x)>0$ (or a separate treatment of $\rho=0$, where $M=0$).

failure_location.quote:
let $V$ be an orthogonal basis for the image of  $ \begin{pmatrix}
      A_xU/\lambda\\ U  \end{pmatrix}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $\rho(A_yA_x)>0$ (equivalently $\ol G^\top A\ol H\ne0$) to the proposition, or handle $\rho=0$ separately (then $M=0$ and $\lambda=0$).
issues.overall_effect: Items 3 and 4 of the proposition are undefined for inputs with $\ol G^\top A\ol H=0$; the proposition is incomplete as stated. Algorithm alg:active_set is unaffected because its skip test $\rho(A_\lambda)\le\lambda^2$ with $\lambda<0$ never applies the proposition in this regime.
issues.title: Construction of V in Proposition pro:sufficient_conditions_feasibility is ill-defined when rho(A_yA_x)=0
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local hypothesis makes the proposition well defined with no mathematical loss, since the algorithmic use never involves $\rho=0$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let  $A_x:=\ol H^+ A^\top\ol G$,  $A_y:=\ol G^+ A\ol H$
$A_\lambda = A_yA_x $, $\wt A_\lambda = A_x$ (or  $A_\lambda = A_xA_y$, $\wt A_\lambda = A_y$ if $|\mathcal I| > |\mathcal J| $).

issues.failure_explanation: With $\ol G\in\R^{m\times|\mathcal I|}$ and $\ol H\in\R^{n\times|\mathcal J|}$, the products $\ol G^+A^\top\ol H$ and $\ol H^+A\ol G$ have incompatible dimensions whenever $m\ne n$, so the step is undefined for rectangular $A$. For $m=n$ with nonsymmetric $A$ the products are defined but differ from $A_y=\ol G^+A\ol H$ and $A_x=\ol H^+A^\top\ol G$ of Proposition pro:sufficient_conditions_feasibility, on which the algorithm's subsequent steps (the test on $\rho(A_yA_x)$, the eigenspace $U$, $W=(\wt A_\lambda U/\mu;U)$ and the $[y;x]$/$[x;y]$ block orders) are based. Executed as written, the algorithm computes candidates from the wrong matrices, so its exactness guarantee fails as printed (the error is masked only when $A$ is symmetric, e.g. $A=I$).

failure_location.quote: $ A_y = \ol G^+ A^\top\ol H$, $A_x = \ol H^+A \ol G$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the line to $A_y=\ol G^+A\ol H$ and $A_x=\ol H^+A^\top\ol G$, matching Proposition pro:sufficient_conditions_feasibility; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The BFAS algorithm's core step is ill-defined for rectangular $A$ and mathematically incorrect for nonsymmetric square $A$ as written; the advertised guarantee of computing an exact solution of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ fails for the algorithm as printed.
issues.title: Algorithm alg:active_set (BFAS) defines A_y and A_x with A and A^top swapped
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction of the two definitions restores the algorithm's exactness guarantee; no proof, enumeration structure or scope needs repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: then compute $a = \sqrt{2n}x = [a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{\lceil(n-1)/2\rceil}]$ and $\lambda = \sqrt 2 y = [\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \dots, \lambda_{\lceil(n-1)/2\rceil}]$

issues.failure_explanation: Under the stated substitution $x=a/\sqrt{2n}$, $y=\lambda/\sqrt2$, the constraint $\|a\|^2=1/(2n)$ maps to $\|x\|^2=1/(4n^2)$ (not $\|x\|^2=1$) and the objective $4\sum a_{k+1}\lambda_j\cos(2\pi jk/n)$ maps to $8\sqrt n\sum x_ky_j\cos(2\pi jk/n)$ (not $\frac{2}{\sqrt n}\sum x_ky_j\cos(2\pi jk/n)$), so the displayed chain of equalities is false as written. The correct substitution is $x=\sqrt{2n}\,a$, $y=\sqrt2\,\lambda$ (i.e. $a=x/\sqrt{2n}$, $\lambda=y/\sqrt2$), under which the final formula and the lemma's statement are correct. The reconstruction text after the lemma repeats the inverted direction ('$a=\sqrt{2n}x$', '$\lambda=\sqrt2 y$'), producing matrices with $\|N\|_F=2n$ and $\|P\|_F=2$ instead of unit norm, so the returned 'optimal solution' is infeasible for the unit-norm constraints (correct only up to scaling, hence the angle itself is right).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the substitution in the proof by $a=x/\sqrt{2n}$, $\lambda=y/\sqrt2$ (equivalently $x=\sqrt{2n}\,a$, $y=\sqrt2\,\lambda$), and correct the reconstruction formulas to $a=x/\sqrt{2n}$, $\lambda=y/\sqrt2$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma lem:equivalence_circulant_SPN_SNN is invalid as written (the equality chain does not follow from the stated substitution), and the post-lemma reconstruction formula returns non-normalized matrices. The lemma's stated equivalence is correct under the proper substitution, and no labelled result depends on the broken step.
issues.title: Inverted change of variables breaks the proof of Lemma lem:equivalence_circulant_SPN_SNN
issues.why_classification: A local inversion of the scaling restores the whole derivation and the reconstruction; the lemma's statement, the matrix $M$ and all downstream numerical uses are unaffected.
